title: When the heart is true
hook: truth is known when the heart is true and falsehood's dirt is washed (Asa di Var, ang 468)

segments.voice: Yesterday, false king, koorh, the passing, and your line: it won't last. What did you notice was still there? Today the very next salok answers koorh with its opposite: sach, truth. Day five hundred forty-nine.

You can tell when a friend is being straight with you. It's not just the words. Their eyes stay on yours, their shoulders aren't braced, there's no little gap between what they say and what they mean. And you can tell the opposite, too, even when every word is technically accurate. Truth, it turns out, isn't only a property of sentences. It's a property of people. Guru Nanak wrote a salok right after yesterday's list of koorh, and it doesn't ask what is true. It asks something harder. When can a person be said to know truth at all?
screen: `A FRIEND BEING STRAIGHT WITH YOU.` → `TRUTH LIVES IN PEOPLE.` → `WHEN DOES A PERSON KNOW IT?`

segments.voice: The salok on ang 468 is built like a ladder, each rung starting the same way: sach taa par jaaneeai. Truth is known only when. Then Guru Nanak fills in the rest. Truth is known when the heart itself is true. When the dirt of falsehood comes off, and the body is washed clean. Truth is known when a person loves truth, when hearing the Name the mind delights, and so finds the door of freedom. Truth is known when a person knows the way to live: making the body into a field and planting the Creator's seed in it. Truth is known when a person takes true teaching, shows kindness to living beings, and gives what they can. Truth is known when a person makes their own self the place of pilgrimage, and settles there, guided by the True Guru. And then the last rung: truth is the medicine for everyone. It washes out wrongdoing. Look at what this list is made of. Not one rung is about winning an argument or holding the right opinion. Every rung is about a person: what the heart loves, how the life is lived, how the hands treat other beings. In Gurbani, sach is both a name for the One and the quality of a life lined up with the One. So a true heart isn't a heart that never makes mistakes. It's a heart with no gap between what it shows and what it is. Yesterday's salok said koorh drowns boatloads. Today's says truth heals everyone. The washing comes first, and it's daily work.
screen: `TRUTH IS KNOWN ONLY WHEN...` · `THE HEART ITSELF IS TRUE.` · `THE BODY A FIELD, THE SEED PLANTED.` · `TRUTH IS MEDICINE FOR ALL.` · then, large: `A TRUE HEART.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: clean one untruth. Sit and let your breathing settle. Look gently for one small gap between what you show and what is: a white lie you've repeated, a promise you made knowing you wouldn't keep it, a version of yourself you've been performing. Pick just one. Picture washing it, the way you'd wash dirt off your hands. Then decide one small, true thing you could say or do about it today. If you pray, you can say Waheguru. The bell holds the time.
When the heart is true. Guru Nanak's ladder of sach: truth is known only when the heart is true, falsehood's dirt is washed, and the life is lived in kindness.
screen: `WHEN THE HEART IS TRUE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: a true heart. Today, do the one true thing you chose, and notice how the body feels afterward. Day five hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Sikhs hear this salok of truth in the dawn singing of Asa di Var, and Sikh teaching holds that truthful living matters even more than knowing the truth.

fork.setup: you want to know truth. according to Guru Nanak's salok, where does it start?
options: in a heart that is itself true, washed of falsehood.
in a long journey to a holy place.
fork.reveal: truth is known only when the heart is true and the dirt of falsehood is washed off. the self becomes the place of pilgrimage.

original.note: Gurmukhi: sach, truth; in Gurbani both a name of the One and a life lined up with the One.

trapdoor: what you thought: a true heart means not telling lies.
what it means: no gap between what you show and what you are, lived in love, kindness and giving.
what a scholar hears: the salok repeats 'sach taa par jaaneeai' as a refrain, answering the koorh salok before it, and ends with truth as medicine for all.

sources.ref: Asa di Var, salok M1 (sach taa par jaaneeai), Ang 468

notes: The salok is paraphrased; confirm the five rungs (true heart and washing; love of truth and the Name; the body as a field with the Creator's seed; true teaching, compassion and giving; the self as pilgrimage place under the True Guru) and the closing 'truth is medicine for all'.
The phrase 'truthful living matters even more than knowing the truth' in howItsDone echoes Sri Rag M1 ('sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar', Ang 62) without quoting; confirm the framing.
